title: Aelix extension catalog
description: An advisory catalog document listing Aelix extensions available to install. The catalog only chooses WHAT to install; the real trust boundary is the install-time consent prompt, verify_and_pin (integrity pin), and the optional Ed25519 signature. Being listed here is NOT an endorsement of safety.
$comment: This schema is a CONTRIBUTOR AID only. The RUNTIME authority is aelix_coding_agent.cli.extension_catalog.parse_catalog, which parses leniently (unknown keys ignored; an entry missing name-or-source, or whose source contains control characters, is silently skipped with a warning). scripts/validate_catalog.py runs parse_catalog and asserts the parsed entry count equals the number of array entries, so a silently-dropped entry fails CI. Where this schema is stricter than parse_catalog (e.g. the sha256 hex pattern), the stricter rule is intentional and applies only in CI.

schemaVersion.description: Catalog document schema version. Only version 1 exists.

name.description: Optional human-readable catalog label shown in the Aelix TUI (e.g. "Aelix official catalog").

updated.description: Optional free-form timestamp for when the catalog was last updated (ISO-8601 recommended).

extensions.description: The list of advertised extensions. Ships empty in the honest starting state.

entry.$comment: additionalProperties is true because parse_catalog preserves unknown keys verbatim (CatalogEntry.extra) for forward compatibility.

name.description: The display + resolve key for the extension. Must be non-empty and free of control characters (control characters are stripped at runtime, and an all-control name is dropped).

source.description: The ONLY field the installer consumes, handed UNCHANGED to `aelix extension install`. THIS catalog admits two forms: (1) a git URL, optionally pinned to a 40-hex commit SHA, e.g. "git+https://github.com/acme/aelix-ext.git" or "git+https://github.com/acme/aelix-ext.git@0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567"; (2) a PyPI package spec, optionally version-pinned, e.g. "aelix-ext-foo" or "aelix-ext-foo==1.2.3". A LOCAL PATH is a third form aelix accepts generally but this catalog REJECTS -- see the $comment below. Must contain no control characters (an entry whose source has a control character is skipped at runtime).
source.$comment: The `not` below rejects the obvious local-path spellings; scripts/verify_candidates.py is the AUTHORITY and rejects the rest (e.g. "extensions/my-ext", which has no leading marker). Why a public catalog cannot list a path at all: aelix's classify_target returns "path" only when the string EXISTS on the machine reading it, so on any machine WITHOUT that directory -- which is every machine but the author's -- the same entry silently stops meaning "this directory" and starts meaning "a package name" nobody chose (aelix-ai #131). It is also unverifiable: the submission gate cannot install a path that is not on the runner. Private and intranet catalogs are unaffected; this rule is this document's, not aelix's.

description.description: Optional short description shown next to the name.

version.description: Optional display version. This is informational only; the installed version is whatever `source` resolves to.

versions.description: Optional list of known versions for display. Informational only.

homepage.description: Optional homepage / repository URL for the extension (https recommended).

sha256.description: ADVISORY, DISPLAY-ONLY lowercase hex SHA-256. This is NEVER a trust signal: it is never written to the integrity pin store and must not be read as "verified". Real integrity comes from the install-time verify_and_pin gate and the optional Ed25519 signature.
